newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere stock rises on plan for debate.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere stock rises on plan for debate.

text.p: Shares in Lagardere group reversed their losses on Tuesday after Prime Minister Alain Juppe said a parliamentary debate on the Thomson privatisation would be held after the privatisation commission announced its decision.

Juppe's announcement follows an outcry from politicians, union leaders and Thomson workers against the proposed sale of Thomson to Lagardere for one franc and the sale of Thomson's TMM consumer electronics unit to Daewoo Electronics of Korea, also for one franc.
Lagardere shares, which fell 6.9 percent on Monday on the growing controversy, were up 0.6 percent at 1330 GMT.
Its stock, which hit a session low earlier of 150.20 francs, swung in a wide range after Juppe's announcement. At 1355 GMT, it was down one percent again.

Traders said there was confusion as to whether Juppe's announcement signalled that the deal might be in jeopardy or whether the debate was being held to allow the government to explain the sale and the terms to quell opposition.
"I don't see them turning back on their decision," a trader said. "I think they're doing this to allow them to respond to criticism and explain their decision."

The government said earlier this month that it preferred Lagardere's bid for Thomson over a rival offer from Alcatel Alsthom, favouring Lagardere's plan to merge its missile unit with Thomson's defence electronics unit Thomson-CSF to create a French defence electronics heavyweight.
It said it would recapitalise debt-saddled Thomson by 11 billion francs before selling it to Lagardere for one franc. Lagardere in turn plans to sell TMM to Daewoo for one franc.
The symbolic sale price generated protests by Thomson workers, union leaders and opposition politicians who criticised the government for throwing away French high-technology.

"Once the (privatisation commission) has delivered its ruling, and whatever its content, I will ask for a public debate on all the issues of this case, financial, industrial and social, so that we can have all the cards on the table before the government decides," Juppe told the French parliament.
The privatisation commission's decision is expected in early December.
